concepts.preferred_label: Severe Heat Stroke with Multi-Organ Dysfunction
concepts.why: The patient's high body temperature, hepatic dysfunction, renal dysfunction, and disseminated intravascular coagulation are consistent with severe heat stroke with multi-organ dysfunction.

The patient's bilateral cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images and decreased perfusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere are consistent with cerebellar infarction.
The patient's disseminated intravascular coagulation is a known complication of severe heat stroke and multi-organ dysfunction.

The patient's low Glasgow Coma Scale score, normal initial head MRI and MRA, and subsequent development of bilateral cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images are consistent with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
It explains the initial normal Head MRI and MRA findings despite subsequent cerebellar abnormalities.

rationales.F12: Decreased perfusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere supports the diagnosis of cerebellar infarction and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome
